chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who married a woman from a people, then found her to be one-eyed, and they had not made that clear to him. Does he return her? He said: “He does not return her. Marriage is only annulled because of insanity, leprosy, and vitiligo.”

I said: What do you think—if he has entered upon her, what should he do? He said: “She is entitled to the dowry because of what he lawfully enjoyed of her private part, and her guardian who married her off must pay him the like of what he gave.”

key_terms.الْبَرَصِ: vitiligo; one of the defects for which annulment is recognized here
key_terms.الْجُذَامِ: leprosy; one of the defects for which annulment is recognized here
key_terms.الْجُنُونِ: insanity; one of the defects for which annulment is recognized here
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: the dowry owed to the wife
key_terms.عَوْرَاءَ: one-eyed; a physical defect mentioned in the case under discussion
key_terms.وَلِيُّهَا: her guardian; the one held financially liable in this case
key_terms.يُرَدُّ النِّكَاحُ: the marriage is annulled or rescinded

ai.seo_question: Can a man annul a marriage if he discovers after marriage that his wife is one-eyed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a marriage in which the husband discovers that the wife is one-eyed after the contract, without prior disclosure. Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام rules that this defect does not permit annulment, and if consummation has occurred, the woman keeps the mahr while her guardian compensates the husband for the amount he paid.
